themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion This Week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 21 THIS WEEK—a 700% jump from the 2.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.22)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapid deterioration of district maintenance in Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 21 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Suggests concentrated problem in specific blocks or corridors within district
reporting_angles: Interview Parks/Sanitation officials: Is this a known crew or spontaneous uptick? What's the response time?
Walk the district to map hotspots—are certain blocks, transit corridors, or landmarks targeted?
Profile small business owners or residents on affected blocks; get photos of before/after

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 93 THIS WEEK—a 356% increase from the 20.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.73)—pointing to either construction activity, street vendor congestion, or traffic enforcement gaps in the district.
evidence: 93 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
356% spike with z-score of 4.73 (highly statistically significant)
Contextual clue: 320 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (236 alterations) may be driving construction noise
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB active permits: Which construction sites correlate with noise complaints?
Interview residents on Flatbush, Coney Island, and nostrand avenues (areas with active rezonings and alterations)
Request DOB enforcement data: Are construction sites violating noise ordinances (e.g., working outside permitted hours)?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 6 LAST WEEK—a staggering 4700% spike from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 17.76)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating either a coordinated poster campaign or complete enforcement breakdown.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)—the single largest z-score anomaly at 17.76
4700% increase represents near-zero baseline exploding to measurable activity
Pattern suggests either new event (concert, political campaign, commercial promotion) or lapsed enforcement
reporting_angles: Map the 6 complaints: Are they clustered on certain corridors (e.g., near transit hubs, retail strips) or dispersed?
Interview Sanitation Department: What triggered the spike? Is it a known event (election, festival, concert) or vigilante posting?
Check for related community complaints on Nextdoor or local Facebook groups—what are residents saying?

themes_detail.label: Plumbing & Construction Surge 2 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged to 76 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 429% jump from the 14.4 weekly average (z-score: 11.3)—correlating with 320 active DOB permits filed in the district and 5 active land-use applications, suggesting major infrastructure or renovation strain.
evidence: 76 construction/plumbing complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 14.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
429% spike with z-score of 11.3 (second-highest statistical anomaly)
Concurrent signal: 320 DOB alteration/new building permits filed in last 90 days; 5 active ULURP/rezoning applications may be driving contractor activity
reporting_angles: Analyze DOB permits filed 2-3 weeks ago: Which projects triggered the construction spike?
Interview DSNY and HPD: Are contractors working without proper permits or licenses? Are inspections keeping pace?
Visit the 5 active rezoning sites (Ditmas Park West, Beverley Square West, three Coney Island/Nostrand/Flatbush Avenue projects): Document construction disruptions

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Encampment-related complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 900% increase from the 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.5)—indicating either new homelessness clusters or deterioration of street conditions in Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 5 encampment complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Suggests concentrated homelessness in specific blocks; no Reddit or news coverage yet, indicating underreported issue
reporting_angles: Map the 5 complaints: Which intersections or parks are encampments clustering? Are they near transit stations or parks?
Interview NYPD and NYC Department of Homeless Services: Are there new encampments in Midwood or along Ocean Parkway? What services exist?
Human interest: Profile residents or small business owners affected by encampments; document safety and sanitation concerns
